title: fix(feishu): acknowledge followups during active work
body:
## Problem and result

Feishu/Lark `/followup` could wait behind active work before reaching admission or reporting queue acceptance. Its retained ingress claim could then block the next message in that chat.

Authorized followups now reach the existing queue while work remains active, receive the runtime’s actual outcome, and execute FIFO under their submitting identity. Ordinary buffered messages retain their ordering. Broadcast observers consume control commands without executing them or leaving retryable ingress behind.

## Implementation

- Supply existing typed command facts before core turn acquisition.
- Release chat-lane occupancy only after the real deferred/adopted/abandoned lifecycle handoff. Durable ingress continues to own recovery custody.
- Consume observer control commands through the existing broadcast lane lifecycle before dispatch. Ordinary observer inference and active-agent admission remain unchanged.
- Run the existing logical-claim abandonment hook before releasing transport custody on stop.

No new queue, authority owner, SDK API, persistence, configuration, or core admission framework. Small existing-owner extractions preserve file-size limits: broadcast claim acquisition, supplemental-context filtering, and command fixtures.

## Behavior and authority proof

**Allowed path (reused):** genuine-human Lark ingress, a real public `gpt-5.4-2026-03-05` model, and isolated AWS Gateways. Against pinned base `06cd3e0`, the first command-facts repair alone left an inherited chat-lane blockage. On `8e75161`, two queue notices arrived **1.789 s / 1.378 s** after submission while the source’s completed provider response remained held. Both durable claims were retained concurrently. Neither followup reached the model early. After release, two distinct executions ran FIFO, each making one exec call and creating its exclusive file once. Actual sender metadata and native requester remained distinct from the WebChat source. Subsequent changes do not alter this path.

The hosted review’s three Before merge requests are addressed as follows:

1. **Unauthorized sender:** actual human Lark group ingress on `3866c10`. The sender could chat but lacked command authorization. `/followup` received the runtime unauthorized-command notice in **1.122 s**, while the source remained held. Its marker reached **0 provider requests**, caused **0 tool effects**, and its ingress completed with **0 retries**. A fresh command after restoring access executed once; the refused command did not revive. No pending inputs remained at shutdown.
2. **Broadcast observer:** **passes on final candidate `d3855e158b355f1588097abf97b0fff46097f60a`.** A fresh isolated AWS Gateway received one genuine-human Lark `/followup`. Provider readback confirms the exact configured human and conversation. One active-agent execution made one exec call and created its exclusive file once; there was **no observer execution, provider request, tool action, or effect**. After graceful shutdown, the sole ingress row is **completed / attempts 0 / no error**, with **0 pending inputs in both agents**. The native message ID appears in the Gateway log and the ingress receive time falls in the observed send window. Completed payload/metadata are cleared by the existing owner; correlation does not infer them from later history. The earlier replay exposed an unadopted observer lane and seven no-op retries; this final replay verifies its repair.
3. **Queued authority:** actual human Lark `/followup` on `3866c10`, acknowledged while the source was held. A tool-only `config.patch` completed its live reload before source release, withdrawing exec/process/write/apply_patch. At admission the queued execution offered **only `session_status`**, made **0 tool actions**, and created **no requested file**. Run and ingress completed; a fresh request after restoration executed once without reviving the restricted request. Ordinary model access remained authorized.

**Applicability:** Feishu’s asserted `plugin:feishu-id` does not confer verified personal-profile operator authority. This is not live Feishu profile-unlink/role-revocation proof, and the PR does not upgrade that trust. Removing configured-owner status alone does not revoke ordinary model access. Existing component tests separately cover committed verified-person unlink/role revocation, current-authority validation during preparation, and terminal consumption of revoked queued input. Already admitted executions retain their prepared permissions.

**Evidence correction:** an initial combined owner-list/tool-policy experiment did not await the completed channel reload and is excluded from passing revocation evidence. Both channel-qualified and id-qualified sender-policy selectors are supported; the successful replay waited for effective application.

## Validation and limits

Final candidate: **107 affected Feishu tests across 6 files** and **5 selected authority tests across 3 files** pass on AWS. Production package-boundary types, scoped test types, typed lint, formatting, test allocation, and full build pass. All **61,191 tracked files** match the commit before/after build and after live shutdown. Independent review and full local ClawSweeper source review found no actionable findings. The full local review covered `4b1ac479726`; its only subsequent change makes three implicit `undefined` returns explicit, independently reviewed and checked. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41117402950) passes; [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41117401598) passes. No main rebase or unrelated CI repair is included.

The observer regression is red on old production (**2 dispatches instead of 1**) and green after repair. It replaces the metadata-only case at the same size, asserting lane/shared custody, no abandonment, and no redelivery execution. Earlier deferred-lane, premature-release-mutant, and stop/replay regressions remain applicable.

Historical `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError` from two earlier attempts remains unexplained; this PR does not claim to fix it. Screenshots, transcript persistence, and model statements are not used as authority proof.

<details>
<summary>Measured costs and LoC churn</summary>

The shared test ceiling is unchanged. The existing exact allocation remains **167 net test lines**, covering command classification, observer settlement, deferred custody, buffering order, and stop cleanup.

| Check | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| Observer regression, expected red before repair | 44.71 s |
| Final affected suite, 107 tests / 6 files | 119.74 s |
| Existing committed unlink/role revocation, 2 selected tests | 74.22 s |
| Existing queued preparation/consumption, 3 selected tests | 75.46 s |
| Production package boundary / typed lint / test types | 30.20 s / 47.31 s / 12.34 s |
| Exact-source full build | 273.16 s |

The final broadcast Gateway ran **100.432 s**: **3 actual model requests**, **17,820 input tokens (7,680 cached)**, **151 output tokens**. Cold transformation dominates the focused suites. The final regression replaces an existing case without increasing its size.

Earlier allowed-path proof: 129.575 s Gateway lifetime, 10 model requests, 58,982 input tokens (31,744 cached), 345 output. Additional unauthorized/broadcast investigation: 10 requests, 57,417 input (28,672 cached), 429 output. Queued-policy work, including the excluded reload experiment: 14 requests, 82,372 input (39,424 cached), 666 output. Monetary spend is not inferred from local zero-valued cost projections.

Against pinned base `06cd3e0f306b`:

| Tests/support | 192 | 25 | 217 |

| Ratchet metadata | 3 | 1 | 4 |
| **Total** | **337** | **100** | **437** |

</details>
